clue.text: Reaction to nitwit on a bender

parts.note: a bender is something that bends, and the joint of the leg is the obvious one
a jerk is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone responds to a fool who is out on a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the nitwit after the bender. A bender is also slang for a drinking binge, which is what the surface wants you to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk is an automatic, unthinking response, like the reflex kick doctors test with a hammer.

clue.text: Take child by hand?

parts.note: surface reading: lead a youngster along holding their hand
setter's reading: carry off a young person by force

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'take' means seize rather than escort; the word's origin is literally kid plus nap, an old word for snatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to abduct someone by force, originally used of stealing children.

clue.text: In my 10 I found hostility

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and recast it, so the letters are poured into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
the numeral spelt out as a word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers ill will at a number they own, perhaps a house or a score.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it is only the word ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is the state of being an enemy, a deep-seated mutual hostility.

clue.text: Flea that dances on mast or bridge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the chigoe, a burrowing tropical flea
second meaning: a small sailing mast at the stern, or the cue rest used in billiards

explanation.surface: An insect hops about the rigging of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The word gathers even more senses: one who dances a jig, the jigger mast, and the billiard cue rest called a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The chigoe flea is also called a jigger, and a jigger is both a small aftermost mast and a billiard bridge.

clue.text: Bring new life to ruler (English) about time!

indicators.note: the ruler and the letter for English go around the period, surrounding it

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch
an era is an age or period of time
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to revive an English monarch at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation of impatience, but 'about' is the container signal and time is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate something is to renew or restore it, giving it fresh vigour and life.

clue.text: Shins of walker with pony?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lower legs, between knee and ankle

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at the phrase for going on foot, not a substitutable synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the legs of a walker, who rides the idiomatic pony meaning one's own feet

explanation.surface: A rambler's lower legs, and a little horse to carry them.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'Shanks's pony' means walking: your own legs are the only pony you ride. The shank is the lower leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanks are the lower parts of the legs between knee and ankle, the same bone region as shins.

clue.text: Front rank of column?

parts.note: the head is the front of a procession or queue
a rank is a line of soldiers standing side by side

explanation.surface: The leading row of soldiers in a marching column.
explanation.walkthrough: Column suggests soldiers on the march, but the whole clue also describes the big-type title line at the top of a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title printed in large type above a newspaper article, its leading line.

clue.text: Nobody got flue? That's an anticlimax!

parts.note: none means not one, nobody
a flue is a duct or vent for smoke

explanation.surface: Nobody caught influenza after all, which is a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Flue looks like a misspelt flu, but it is the chimney duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is an occasion that fails to live up to expectations, a disappointing anticlimax.

clue.text: A few people have rest disturbed in the south-west

definitions.note: names where the county lies rather than the county itself

parts.note: some means a few

indicators.note: rest that is disturbed is broken up, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A handful of holidaymakers in the West Country sleep badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county in the south-west, home to Glastonbury and Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county located in the south-west of England, so the clue defines it by position.

clue.text: Rabble-rousing needs a giant in paper size

indicators.note: the article and the giant are placed inside the paper size, so 'in' signals one thing set within another

parts.note: demy is a traditional size of printing and writing paper
taken as written
Gog is one of the legendary giants, paired with Magog, guarding the City of London

explanation.surface: Stirring up a mob calls for a huge sheet of newsprint.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMY is a paper size; Gog and Magog are the giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Demagogy is the practice of winning support by inflaming the prejudices and passions of the crowd.

clue.text: Showman, the greatest, not counting the miners

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'bar none'
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

explanation.surface: A boastful performer claims top billing once the miners are left out of the count.
explanation.walkthrough: P. T. Barnum billed his circus as 'The Greatest Show on Earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phineas Taylor Barnum was the famous American circus impresario, known as the greatest showman of his age.

clue.text: Listen: he goes in last

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the word for listen, sitting within it

parts.note: to attend is to pay heed or listen
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention: a man takes his turn at the back of the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done last is done finally, in the closing position after everything else.

clue.text: With art, the classical's always with it

parts.note: cl. is the standard abbreviation for classical
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: An art lover insists classical taste never goes out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Art here is skill or cunning, as in artful; 'with it' only ties the abbreviation to the adverb that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with art means acting with skill and ingenuity, which is being clever.

clue.text: French settlers in remarkable victory in another of their old colonies

indicators.note: the settlers are placed inside the rearranged word
a remarkable thing is out of the ordinary, so these letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
the OAS was the paramilitary organisation of French settlers fighting Algerian independence

explanation.surface: Colonists from France win a triumph in yet another territory they once ruled.
explanation.walkthrough: The OAS, Organisation armée secrète, was the settlers' underground army in French Algeria; 'another' nods to Algeria as one colony and the answer as another.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory Coast, now Côte d'Ivoire, was a French colony in West Africa until independence in 1960.

clue.text: Article in part of France where it came from

indicators.note: the article sits inside the French region, so 'in' marks the insertion

parts.note: Provence is the region of south-east France
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a word in a southern French region, and an object's place of origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is an object's origin or recorded history, especially for art and antiques.

clue.text: Aubergine, for example, in great little scheme

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the scheme sits inside the short form of great

parts.note: a little great is its abbreviation, gt
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A vegetable features in a grand but modest plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like part of the definition, Aubergine being an example of something, but it supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggplant is the American name for the aubergine, the purple fruit used as a vegetable.

clue.text: Punishment with two stripes?

definitions.note: adjective in the phrase corporal punishment, not a noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: bodily, as in physical chastisement of the body
second meaning: the army rank whose sleeve badge has two chevrons

explanation.walkthrough: Stripes could be lashes, but they are the chevrons on a non-commissioned officer's sleeve; the same word describes punishment of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal wears two chevrons in the British Army, and corporal punishment is physical beating.

clue.text: Hair style raised remark at harvest

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a note is a brief remark
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: Someone comments on the size of this year's yield.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton crop was a short, slicked-down women's haircut fashionable in the 1920s, named after Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton crop was a very short boyish hairstyle for women popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Tale written by another (?) gives good numbers to Conservative

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
hosts are multitudes, large numbers of people
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A ghost-written account hands a Tory politician plenty of supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on ghost-writing, a book written by another under someone else's name; the question mark flags that the tale is really of the spooky kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale about spirits is a ghost story, and a ghostwritten book is one penned by another person.

clue.text: An acid with relation to 1099

parts.note: bro is short for brother
in Roman numerals M is 1000 and IC, a loose form, is 99

explanation.surface: A chemistry fact about a compound linked to a date just after the Norman Conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 99 is XCIX in Roman numerals; the setter uses the shortcut IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromic acid, HBrO3, is an oxoacid of bromine, so the word names an acid.

clue.text: Little change to little dance

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: minute means tiny, very little

explanation.surface: A small adjustment is made to a short dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters swap. The second 'little' is a nod to the name's origin, French menuet, small, for its tiny steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately ballroom dance for couples in triple time, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: High and low ground, one might hear, between barrels?

indicators.note: what one might hear is the spoken form, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: high, then fen, flat low-lying marshland

explanation.surface: Hills and valleys lie between the barrels in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's checked letters fit, but the answer was guessed as SYPHON; the sound and the double-barrelled-name definition give HYPHEN, whose first and fifth letters are unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-barrelled surname like Smith-Jones has a hyphen joining its two barrels.

clue.text: Very hot mass of metal with fastening inside

indicators.note: the fastening sits inside the lump of metal, held within it

parts.note: a pig is an oblong mass of cast iron from a smelter
a pin fastens things together

explanation.surface: A lump of metal fresh from the furnace has a bolt fixed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot food is steaming and very hot, from the hiss or whistle of something boiling.

clue.text: Famine will cause prolonged damage to town

parts.note: a scar is lasting damage left behind
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Hunger leaves a community lastingly harmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Famine is an extreme shortage of food, so scarcity is a fair general synonym.

clue.text: Heavenly lights of gold in atmosphere

indicators.note: the heraldic metal is placed inside the word for atmosphere

parts.note: an aura is a distinctive atmosphere around a place or person
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Golden glows high up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a common crossword convention; AU, the chemical symbol, is a tempting false path but leaves the wrong letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis and australis are shimmering displays of coloured light across the night sky.

clue.text: In his salad days, member for great seaside town

indicators.note: the limb is put inside the word for those early years

parts.note: salad days are one's youthful, inexperienced years
a member is a limb

explanation.surface: A young politician sits as the MP for a large resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Yarmouth is a Norfolk resort on England's east coast, so 'great' is part of its name, not mere praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarmouth, properly Great Yarmouth, is a well-known English seaside resort in Norfolk.

clue.text: You French speakers make bloomers

parts.note: tu is French for you
lips are what we speak with

explanation.surface: French people talking make embarrassing mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers looks like blunders or knickers, but it means things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring flowers, and anything that blooms can be called a bloomer in crosswords.

clue.text: Standard weight on Teesside

parts.note: stock means standard or regular, as in a stock reply
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A regular measure of weight used in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockton-on-Tees is a town in north-east England; the definition is the place's position on that river.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton-on-Tees is a town on the River Tees, part of the Teesside conurbation in north-east England.
